newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-UNFANCIED VALLADOLID CLINCH UEFA CUP PLACE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-UNFANCIED VALLADOLID CLINCH UEFA CUP PLACE.

text.p: With Real Madrid already installed as league champions, unfancied Valladolid clinched one of Spain's remaining two UEFA Cup places with a 1-0 win over Hercules on Sunday.
Valladolid secured their European place, the third in their history, on a 33rd minute goal by Jose Quevedo.

Athletic Bilbao need to beat Deportivo Coruna on Monday to secure the last place in Europe after Basque rivals Real Sociedad kept their own outside hopes alive with two late goals in a 2-1 win at Compostela.
Real Madrid had taken their 27th league championship by beating neighbours Atletico 3-1 in an impressive demonstration on Saturday.
Some 800,000 fans took to the streets of the Spanish capital to celebrate the victory.
But the Real players had their festivities muted by news of the death in a household accident of the six-year old son of club doctor Alfonso del Corral.
Several club officials, among them manager Fabio Capello, attended the boy's funeral on Sunday afternoon.
Capello had announced after the game that he will return to AC Milan next season, but did not comment on the future of Arrigo Sacchi, current manager of the Italian side.
Real president Lorenzo Sanz said he is close to reaching an agreement with Tenerife coach Jupp Heynckes to replace Capello.
Real's victory meant that Barcelona's game with Betis was no more than a dress rehearsal for June 28's Spanish Cup final.
But in the case of one fan it wasn't even that -- as the highlight of a dull game was the appearance of a streaker.
Barcelona took the match 3-0 with goals from Oscar Garcia, Hristo Stoichkov and Luis Enrique Martinez.
Fans in the Camp Nou carried a banner reading "No more foreigners who don't feel the colours".
At the other end of the table, Sporting Gijon beat Rayo Vallecano 3-0 to lift themselves out of danger and leave Rayo deep in trouble.
Needing to win to escape certain relegation, Extremadura dispatched fellow strugglers Celta Vigo 2-0.
Extremadura, Celta, Rayo, Oviedo and Espanyol will face the final weekend of league action fighting either automatic relegation or a play-off against Mallorca.
Mallorca finished third in the second division, which concluded on Sunday.

Fourth-placed Eibar receive 150 million pesetas ($1.03 million) as compensation for staying in the second division. The reduction of the first division from 22 to 20 teams means that only two sides will be automatically promoted, while four are relegated.
Salamanca on Sunday joined champions Merida as one of the two teams to win a place in the first divsion.
Both sides bounce back to the top flight after being relegated last year.
